IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGER: inference-prod GPU capacity degraded. Autoscaling not keeping up, request queue growing on inference-worker. Suspected HPA/custom metrics pipeline lag (prometheus -> custom-metrics-adapter). Paging oncall.

Maya S.: I'm oncall — ack. Jumping in. Any immediate customer impact?

Devon L.: Seeing queue depth spike on the frontend metrics: avg_queue_depth -> 1200 (baseline <200). Throttles at the allocator layer started returning 429s. Logs show HPA target metrics stale for ~7m.

Raj P.: Can you pull adapter logs? I want to see scrape errors and upstream 5xxs.

Devon L.: metrics-adapter (kube-system/custom-metrics-adapter) shows repeated: 
```
E0305 06:11:02 1 storage_adapter.go:123] failed to fetch metrics from prometheus: GET https://prometheus.kube-system.svc/api/v1/query?query=custom:queue_depth:rate(5m) -> 502 Bad Gateway
```
Retries then backoff. Prometheus cluster shows high TSDB write latency, remote_write backlog.

Olivia K.: Prometheus node cpu/IO high on prometheus-0. We've had a big spike in scrape cardinality since the new rollout of per-route metrics yesterday. Could be causing query timeouts to the adapter.

Maya S.: For immediate mitigation: 1) scale HPA target manually so we don't rely on adapter; 2) reduce scrape cardinality or pause the new per-route job; 3) if needed, move a portion of traffic to dedicated-runtime pool. Which is lowest-effort now?

Raj P.: Manual scale first. Run: 
```
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/inference-worker --replicas=20
kubectl patch hpa inference-worker -n inference --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":20}}'
```
That buys headroom while we fix metrics path.

Devon L.: Doing the scale now. `kubectl scale` returned success. Pods coming up (5/20 ready).

MetricsBot: autoscaler: HPA target metrics not found for 7m, using fallback replica count.

Maya S.: Routing change — can we shift low-priority traffic to dedicated pool? We should avoid shifting ALL traffic because some customers rely on inference-prod regional affinity.

Olivia K.: I can flip a canary rule to send experimental workloads to dedicated-runtime: `trafficctl promote routing-rule/perf-test -> dedicated-runtime`. Doing that for the heavy batch jobs. :white_check_mark:

Devon L.: Prometheus pod restarted once to reclaim disk pressure, but it came back with high query latency. I truncated the most expensive per-route metric in the TSDB temporarily: `curl -X POST http://prometheus-0:9090/api/v1/admin/tsdb/drop_series -d 'match[]=per_route_latency{env=\"prod\"}'` (we used the admin endpoint). Query latency improved slightly.

Raj P.: Good call. Next steps: 1) revert the per-route scrape rollout (disable new relabel configs) 2) restart custom-metrics-adapter after prometheus stabilizes 3) monitor HPA metrics for recovery.

Maya S.: Customer impact: we've observed increased 429s and elevated latency for ~18% of requests to inference-prod between 06:08-06:35 UTC. I notified support and flagged top 5 customers with SLO risk. Ticket #INC-3142 opened.

Olivia K.: Rolling back the per-route scrape job now. Command: `kubectl -n monitoring delete cronjob/per-route-scrape-test` — removed.

MetricsBot: Prometheus query latency 95p dropped from 8s -> 1.2s within 4m after drop_series and job removal.

Devon L.: Restarting custom-metrics-adapter now to pick up healthy prometheus responses: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/custom-metrics-adapter
```
Adapter came up and is serving metrics again. HPA started seeing metrics within 90s.

Maya S.: Observed HPA scaling activity: replicas increased from 6 -> 18 automatically. Queue depth trending down.

Raj P.: Keep an eye on node GPU utilization. If we hit node packing limits we'll need to temporarily increase node pool max or spin up extra GPU nodes: 
```
gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize ig-gpu-workers --size=40 --zone=us-west1-a
```
(Only run if pods remain pending for >10m).

Maya S.: For the immediate oncall log: mitigation steps executed: manual scale, removed high-cardinality scrapes, restarted prometheus, restarted adapter, traffic shifted for non-critical jobs. Customer impact documented in INC-3142.

Olivia K.: Confirmed: no pods pending, GPU utilization ~78% across cluster. Queue depth back to ~140. Throttles dropped to near-zero.

Raj P.: Postmortem action items (brief): 1) rollback safe guard for per-route metrics rollout (feature gate + canary fraction), 2) autoscaler fallback improvement (better local fallback heuristics when adapter stale), 3) prometheus autoscaling / storage relief for spikes, 4) run drills for manual scale and traffic shift. I'll own 1 & 2.

Maya S.: Handoff: I'm ending shift in 30m and handing oncall to Raj. Please watch for any regressions.

Raj P.: Taking over. Thanks all. Please add any customer follow-ups to INC-3142 and tag me. :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: Incident resolved for now — monitoring continues.

Maya S.: Summary for post-incident notes: root cause was high-cardinality scrape introduced yesterday causing Prometheus query timeouts -> custom-metrics-adapter errors -> HPA metrics stale -> delayed autoscaling -> queue growth and throttling. Mitigations: manual scale, remove offending scrape, restart services, traffic steering. Next: more conservative rollout and autoscaler fallback.

Olivia K.: Adding dashboard snapshots and relevant logs to the incident ticket.

Devon L.: Leaving a copy of the commands used in case we need to replay. :lock:

Raj P.: Logging runbook updates now. Will schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow.

Maya S.: :white_check_mark: closing thread here, leaving monitoring on for 2h then will close INC-3142 if stable.
